passage: I'm Ayesha, and I was waiting in the ticket line at the bus station on Sunday. Pankaj, who I recognised from my college, strolled up the side and slipped in three places ahead, with a quick "Just one ticket." A few people frowned but said nothing. A woman with two bags behind him said, calmly, "The line starts back there, please." Pankaj hesitated. His ears turned red, and he shrugged and walked to the end, where he stood scrolling his phone. I don't know if he was annoyed or embarrassed. Later, he nodded at me and said, "Fair enough." The line moved on.

qa.q: How many places ahead did Pankaj slip into the line?
qa.a: Pankaj slipped in three places ahead.

qa.q: What might Pankaj have been feeling when his ears turned red?
qa.a: Pankaj was probably embarrassed or annoyed at being called out, though the narrator says it cannot be known.

qa.q: What made the woman's request effective?
qa.a: She spoke calmly and politely, saying where the line starts, and did not shout or insult him, so Pankaj could go back without a fight.

qa.q: How might the people in the line have felt when Pankaj slipped ahead?
qa.a: A few frowned but stayed silent, which suggests they felt annoyed but did not want a scene.

grounding: A young adult slips ahead in a ticket line and calmly being asked to join the back of the line works.

passage:
Monday: At the exam-form counter, Kashish saw a long line and slipped in beside her friend near the front, murmuring, "Just a minute." People behind her looked away.
Tuesday: The queue was long again. Saurabh, standing in front of the spot where she tried to slip in, said politely, "The line starts there, Kashish." Her cheeks went hot. She walked to the back.
Wednesday: Kashish arrived early and stood in the line without a word. When she reached the counter, the clerk smiled. Saurabh, two places behind, gave her a thumbs up.

qa.q: On which day did Saurabh speak to Kashish about the line?
qa.a: Saurabh spoke to her on Tuesday.

qa.q: What was Kashish feeling when Saurabh said the line starts there?
qa.a: Kashish felt embarrassed, since her cheeks went hot, before walking to the back.

qa.q: What changed for Kashish between Monday and Wednesday?
qa.a: After being asked politely, Kashish walked to the back on Tuesday and arrived early to stand in line on Wednesday.

qa.q: How might Saurabh have felt when speaking up?
qa.a: Saurabh spoke politely and gave a thumbs up later, so Saurabh probably wanted fairness for others without shaming Kashish.

grounding: A young adult slips ahead in a queue, and calmly being asked to join the back of the line works and trust stays.
